production.format_and_medium.summary: If requested, the entity must provide a copy in an electronic format by electronic medium, unless the record was neither created nor available electronically, or doing so would give access to proprietary software or require producing non-separable confidential information.
A custodian must not refuse to provide a copy in the requested medium because it has already prepared, or would prefer to provide, the copy in a different medium.

production.delivery_and_completion.summary: On request, the custodian must prepare the copy of the record and must not require the requester to prepare the copy himself or herself.

production.certified_copy.summary: An officer having custody of non-confidential public records must furnish certified copies to any person who requests them and pays or tenders the prescribed copying/certifying fees.

eligibility.any_person.summary: All public books and records of a governmental entity must be open during office hours to inspection by any person, and may be fully copied.

eligibility.no_purpose_requirement.summary: Access runs to 'any person'; the statute requires no statement of purpose or justification for a request.

eligibility.no_residency_requirement.summary: Access runs to 'any person'; the statute imposes no residency or citizenship condition on who may request public records.

fee.waiver.summary: A governmental entity may waive all or part of a copy fee if it adopts a written waiver policy and posts a legible sign or notice of the policy's terms at each office providing copies.

When a public record copy is required by the federal Department of Veterans Affairs to determine benefit eligibility, the custodian must provide a certified copy without charge to the applicant, their representative, or the VA.

custody.referral_to_proper_custodian.summary: If the entity does not have legal custody or control of the record, it must provide written notice of that fact and the name and address of the entity that does have custody or control, if known.

clarification.duty_to_assist.summary: When unable to produce by day five, the entity must make a reasonable effort to assist the requester to focus the request to maximize the likelihood of obtaining the record as expeditiously as possible.

response.initial_decision_window.summary: Not later than the end of the fifth business day after receipt of a request, the entity must allow inspection/copying or provide the copy (or give one of the alternative statutory responses).
response.initial_decision_window.clock_spec: 5 business-days from custodian's receipt of request

response.extension_notice.summary: If unable to make the record available by the end of the fifth business day, the entity must give the requester written notice of that fact and the earliest date and time the entity reasonably believes the record will be available.
response.extension_notice.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "earliest date and time after which the governmental entity reasonably believes" the record will be available, from the end of the 5th business day

production.completion_window.summary: If a record is readily available for inspection or copying, the custodian must allow the requester to inspect, copy or receive a copy as expeditiously as practicable.
production.completion_window.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "as expeditiously as practicable" from receipt of request

production.completion_window.summary: When a county recorder receives a request for a particular item that has been removed to storage, the recorder must produce a microfilmed copy or the original within three working days.
production.completion_window.clock_spec: 3 working-days from county recorder's receipt of request

fee.copy_rate_per_page.summary: A governmental entity may charge a fee for a copy, but the fee must not exceed the actual cost to provide the copy unless a specific statute or regulation sets the fee.
fee.copy_rate_per_page.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost of providing the copy

fee.actual_cost_basis.summary: 'Actual cost' means direct cost of providing the copy (ink, toner, paper, media, postage) and excludes any cost the entity incurs regardless of whether a copy is requested.

fee.electronic_media_charge.summary: A fee for information from a geographic information system may include, in addition to actual medium cost, the reasonable costs of data gathering/entry, database maintenance, hardware, software, quality control, and consultation with personnel.

fee.nonstandard_rate.summary: The fee for a copy of a record in the custody of a governmental law library must not exceed 50 cents per page.

For a copy of a certified-court-reporter transcript of an administrative proceeding, the entity must charge, on top of actual medium cost, a per-page fee equal to the court reporter's contract per-page fee, and remit that amount to the reporter.
fee.nonstandard_rate.clock_spec: fixed: court reporter's contract per-page fee + actual medium cost

fee.no_charge_categories.summary: A governmental entity must not charge a fee for a copy if a specific statute or regulation requires it to provide the copy without charge.
